denial.falsifier: Any C source form, or any per-Object cflags variant, that simultaneously (a) exports the four names from atree.o and (b) leaves all 36 functions at real 0 -- in particular any form that puts a 1-byte-aligned 0x180 object BETWEEN two 4-byte-aligned 0x60 objects in MWCC's .bss emission, which is what the target layout requires and which no ordering key can produce.
denial.premise_measurement: TWO facts that cannot both be satisfied by any C source under this compiler. (1) LINKAGE IS REQUIRED: `objdump -r build/GUNE5D/obj/game/pb/pb_diag.o` prints `R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO whichatree` at 0x12e2/0x12ee, `... atree_handles` at 0x1312/0x1316, `... atree_scroll` at 0x15d6/0x15da and `R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 natreelists` at 0x11bc, so atree.o must EXPORT all four or the link fails (the predecessor measured that failure verbatim). (2) THE TARGET LAYOUT IS UNREACHABLE FROM GLOBALS: the target addresses all three arrays from ONE base, `@0x20 lis r3,0 @atree_handles(ADDR16_HA)` / `@0x24 addi r28,r3,0 @atree_handles(ADDR16_LO)` then `@0x8c8 stw r31,480(r3)` and `@0x8d4 stb r0,96(r3)` off r28, i.e. atree_handles +0, atree_scroll +0x60, whichatree +0x1E0 -- DECLARATION order. Under `static` MWCC merges them into the anonymous `...bss.0` block at exactly those offsets and fn_8001267C is byte-identical to target (real 72 raw, closed by its shipped rule). Under external linkage MWCC emits three separate .bss objects at whichatree +0, atree_handles +0x60, atree_scroll +0xC0, and `objdump -t build/GUNE5D/src/game/anim/.postprocess/body/atree.o` prints that SAME order for BOTH declaration orders tried and for `-common off`, so the order is a function of the objects' intrinsic keys and not of source order (see claim.law.FQ_mwcc-orders-uninitialised-file-scope-globals-by-an-intrinsic-key-source-order-cannot-change.20260903.v1). Measured cost of globalization, `fndiff game/anim/atree.c --raw --count`: fn_8001267C real 72 -> 82, every other function unchanged (DoAnimateTreeFrame 38, fn_80011BBC 6, AtreeInitSub 38, all 32 others real 0) -- reproducing the predecessor's number exactly. The single-aggregate form (probe D) DOES restore fn_8001267C to real 72 and gives one exported 0x240-byte .bss symbol, but it hands MWCC the field-offset knowledge the target does NOT have in AtreeModel: target `@0x2c lis r3,0 @atree_handles(ADDR16_HA)` RELOADS the base inside the loop for a second named object, ours CSEs it off the struct base, and the cost is AtreeModel 20/17 insns real 15, fn_80011BBC 88/87 real 53, AtreeInitLists real 2 -- three previously byte-exact functions demoted.
